(And from the mode of allusion (ishara) in the verses) ﴿Allah made the Ka'ba, the Sacred House...﴾ It is, according to them, the Presence of Unity (hadrat al-jam'), forbidden to outsiders (aghyar). It was said: the heart of the believer. It was said: the specific Ka'ba, not in terms of being four walls and a roof, but in terms of being the locus of manifestation of Allah's majesty, may He be exalted. They have mentioned that He, glorified be He, manifests Himself from it to the eyes of the knowers (arifin), as indicated by His saying, mighty is His state, in what is in the Torah: "Allah came from Sinai, appeared from Se'ir, and shone forth from Paran." ﴿A means of standing for mankind﴾ from their true death, due to what results for them through it. ﴿And the sacred month﴾, which is the time of arrival, or the observance of the heart, or attaining that manifestation in which the manifestation of the attributes of the soul is forbidden, or turning toward the demands of the natural faculties, or the like. ﴿And the offering﴾, which is the soul slaughtered through annihilation in the presence of unity, or the divine inflows that come to the heart, or what the servant receives of favours at that manifestation. ﴿And the garlands﴾, which are the noble submissive soul, or a kind of what the servant receives from his Master, leading him forcibly away from the straight path. ﴿That is so that you may know﴾ through what results for you ﴿that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of everything.﴾ That is, He knows the realities of things in the worlds of the unseen and the witnessed, and His knowledge encompasses everything. ﴿Say: The corrupt and the good are not equal﴾ among souls, deeds, morals, and wealth, ﴿even if the abundance of the corrupt impresses you﴾ because of its suitability to the soul. For the first is a cause of nearness, unlike the second. ﴿O you who have believed﴾ with demonstrative faith (iman burhani), ﴿do not ask﴾ of the possessors of eyewitness faith (iman 'ayani) ﴿about things﴾ that are unseen and realities that are not known except through unveiling ﴿which, if they were shown to you, would distress you﴾, that is, would destroy you because of your deficiency in knowing them, so that would be a cause of your denial. Allah, glorified be He, is jealous, and He becomes angry for His friends as the lion becomes angry for war. In this, as it has been said, is a warning to the novices (ahl al-bidaya) against their excessive questioning of the perfected ones about the secrets of the unseen, and a guidance for them to companionship with submission. ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed﴾, which comprises the outward and the inward and contains what you were asked about, ﴿they will be shown to you﴾ through it. ﴿Allah did not appoint any bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham﴾. The bahira is the soul whose ear was slit for hearing what is contrary (to the law). The sa'iba is the soul released from restraint, roaming in the gardens of desires. The wasila is the soul which connected the ropes of its hopes to one another, and so postponed repentance and preparation for the Hereafter. The ham is one who was occupied for a time with obedience, but the door of arrival was not opened to him, so Satan whispered to him and said: "What you have done suffices you; there is nothing beyond what you are in, so rest your soul," and he thus restrained his soul from bearing the hardships of striving (mujahadat).

Al-Nishapuri related from Shaykh Najm al-Din, known as Daya, that the bahira is an allusion to the Haydariyya and the Qalandariyya, who pierce their ears, put iron rings in them, and abandon the Shari'a. The sa'iba is an allusion to those who wander the earth, casting off excuses without the bridle of the Shari'a and the fetter of the path, and claim that they are people of the Reality (haqiqa). The wasila is an allusion to the people of permissiveness (ibaha) who connect with strangers by way of brotherhood and union, and reject companionship with relatives for the sake of partisanship and obstinacy. The ham is an allusion to the one deluded by Allah, mighty and majestic, who thinks he has reached the station of Reality, so the violation of the Shari'a does not harm him. ﴿And when it is said to them: "Come to what Allah has sent down"﴾ of rulings ﴿and to the Messenger"﴾ to follow him, ﴿they say: "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon"﴾ of actions by which they lived and died. ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing﴾ of the Shari'a or the path, ﴿and were not guided﴾ to the Reality?

﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves﴾, so occupy yourselves with purifying them. ﴿Those who have strayed will not harm you﴾ from what you are upon, when they object to you, ﴿once you have been guided﴾ and have purified your souls. The harm of that falls only upon their own selves.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, the witness among you...﴾ the two verses, nothing appeared to the servant in it that is suitable for editing, and al-Nishapuri, in applying it to what is in the souls, mentioned what I see as more precious to leave alone. ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the Messengers﴾, which is the Great Day of Resurrection, ﴿and He will say﴾ to them: ﴿"What were you answered?"﴾ when you called the creation. ﴿They will say: "We have no knowledge"﴾ of that ﴿You are the Knower of the unseen"﴾, so You know the answer to what we were asked. This, as it has been said, is at the accumulation of the onslaughts of majesty and the manifestation of the mantle of greatness and the garment of magnificence; therefore they will be astonished, bewildered, perplexed, and dissolved. For Allah, glorified be He, there are manifestations upon the people of His nearness and the possessors of His love: He annihilates them at times through majesty, and leaves them subsisting for a while through beauty; He addresses them once with gentleness and treats them another time with subjugation, and everything the Beloved does is beloved.

Some of the people of interpretation (ta'wil) said: Allah will gather the Messengers in the very unity of the Absolute Unity (al-jam' al-mutlaq) or the very unity of the Essence (jam' al-dhat), and He will ask them: "Did you have insight into the stations of creation in their perfections when you called them to Me?" Then they will negate knowledge from themselves and affirm it for Allah, exalted is He, because the station of annihilation requires that. ﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother"﴾ for the beloved ones and the seekers, ﴿so that their desire for Me may increase, and be grateful for that, so that I may increase you from what I have. For My treasuries are filled with what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.﴾ ﴿When I supported you with the Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus)﴾, which is the Spirit that shone forth from the dawn of pre-eternity, and it is His pure spirit. It was said: what is meant is "I supported you with Gabriel," since he taught you the marks of servanthood. ﴿You spoke to people in the cradle﴾, that is, in the cradle of the body, or in the well-known cradle, meaning: you spoke to them as a child, glorifying Allah, exalted is He, and affirming to Him servanthood. ﴿And in maturity﴾, that is, in the state of your old age. What is meant is that your state did not differ between childhood and old age; rather your glorification of your Lord continued, and you did not turn back. ﴿When I taught you the Book﴾, which is the book of realities and gnoses, ﴿and wisdom﴾, which is the wisdom of traveling to Allah, mighty and majestic, through acquiring morals, states, stations, detachment, and singling out. ﴿And the Torah﴾, that is, the outward sciences and the rulings concerning actions and the states and attributes of the soul. ﴿And the Gospel﴾, the inward sciences, among which is knowledge of the manifestations of the attributes and the rulings concerning the states and attributes of the heart. ﴿When you shape﴾ by nurturing or by fashioning ﴿from clay﴾, which is pure preparedness, or the well-known clay, ﴿in the form of a bird﴾, that is, like the image of the bird of the heart flying toward the presence of holiness, or the well-known bird, ﴿and you breathe into it﴾ from the outward spirit within you, ﴿and it becomes a bird﴾, a pure soul flying with the wing of purity and love, or a real bird, ﴿by My permission﴾, since you became a manifestor of Me. ﴿And you heal the blind﴾, that is, the one veiled from the light of the Truth, ﴿and the leper﴾, that is, the one whose heart has been corrupted by love of the world and dominance of desire, ﴿by My permission. And when you bring forth the dead﴾ with the disease of ignorance from the graves of nature ﴿by My permission. And when I restrained the Children of Israel﴾, who are the carnal faculties, or those veiled from the light of the manifestations of the attributes, ﴿from you﴾, so their plotting did not diminish you at all, ﴿when you came to them with clear proofs﴾, which are the manifest arguments, or the dominant spiritual faculties; ﴿and when I inspired﴾ by way of inspiration (ilham) ﴿the disciples﴾, who are those who purified their souls with the water of beneficial knowledge and cleansed the garments of their hearts from the defilement of natures, ﴿saying: "Believe in Me"﴾ with true faith in the unity of the attributes, ﴿and in My Messenger"﴾ by observing the rights of their manifestations in detail.

Some of the masters mentioned that inspiration is of two kinds: special and general. The special is that which occurs without an intermediary, and the general is that which occurs through an intermediary, such as an angel, the spirit, the heart, the intellect, the secret, and the movement of the primordial nature (fitra). The saints (awliya') have a share in this second kind. The special inspiration has degrees: the inspiration of the act (wahy al-fi'l) and the inspiration of the essence (wahy al-dhat). The inspiration of the essence occurs in the station of unity, at the vision of greatness and majesty, and the inspiration of the act occurs in the station of passionate love and affection, and there are the stations of intimacy and expansiveness. ﴿When the disciples said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?"﴾, that is, the Lord who nurtures you and bestows upon you what perfected you, ﴿a table﴾, that is, a law comprising kinds of sciences, wisdoms, gnoses, and rulings, ﴿from heaven﴾, that is, from the direction of the heaven of spirits. ﴿He said: "Fear Allah"﴾, that is, make Him, glorified be He, your protection in what proceeds from you of actions and morals, ﴿if you are believers"﴾, and do not ask for a new law. ﴿They said: "We want to eat from it"﴾, by acting upon it, ﴿and that our hearts may be at rest"﴾, for knowledge is nourishment, ﴿and that we may know that you have been truthful with us"﴾ in reports about your Lord and about yourself, ﴿and that we may be among the witnesses to it"﴾, so that we may inform the absent ones through it and call them to it. ﴿He said: "Allah said: I will send it down to you. Whoever among you disbelieves afterwards﴾ in it and veils himself from that religion, ﴿afterwards"﴾, that is, after the sending down, ﴿I will punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds."﴾ That is through veiling from Me, because of the presence of the preparedness, the clarity of the path, and the shining forth of the proof. Punishment with knowledge is more severe than punishment with ignorance. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to people..."﴾ and so on, is the speech of the Greatest Shaykh (al-Shaykh al-Akbar), may his secret be sanctified. The speech of Shaykh 'Abd al-Karim al-Jili is famous and widespread on the tongues of the sincere and the deniers among us. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best His intent. We ask Allah, exalted is He, to send down upon us tables of His generosity, not to cut off from us the habits of His blessings, and to be gentle with us at the beginning and the end, by the sanctity of our Prophet, upon whom be the best of prayers and the most complete of peace.
